group: A research association says that, across a group of people, a trait and a reading moved together on average. It is not a measurement of you, and it does not predict anything about you.
gene: A gene is a stretch of DNA that carries the recipe for one protein. A change in the recipe can change the protein.
het: You carry two copies of most genes, one from each parent. One altered copy means the other copy is unchanged.
hom: Both copies of the gene carry the change.
dominant: One altered copy is enough to raise the chance of the condition.
recessive: Two altered copies are needed for the condition. One altered copy makes a carrier, who does not usually have the condition.
plp: A laboratory classification of the change itself. It says the change can cause the condition. It does not say the condition is present.
vus: Laboratories do not yet know what this change does.
stars: ClinVar's 0 to 4 scale for how well laboratories agree. 2 stars means several laboratories agree with the same criteria. 4 means a practice guideline.
af: How often a change appears among sampled chromosomes in a reference population. Rare does not mean harmful.
or: How many times higher the odds of a trait were in people with the allele, compared with people without it, in one study.
beta: How much a measured trait moved, on average, per copy of the allele, in one study.
p: How unlikely the study result would be if there were no real association. Smaller is stronger. It says nothing about the size of the effect.
prediction: A computer model's estimate, not a laboratory classification. Models are wrong often enough that a prediction alone is not a result.
array: A consumer test that reads a fixed set of positions. It misreads rare changes often, so a rare pathogenic call from an array needs a clinical test.
methylation: A chemical mark on DNA that changes with age, tissue, exposure and disease. A reading is a value from 0 to 1 for one site.
